# How to Calculate Profit and Loss for Futures Contracts

Published on 2021-07-26 02:57

Updated on 2026-02-02 11:08

Profit and loss calculations are based on the contract’s collateral. For example, a USDⓈ-margined contract is denominated in USDT, whereas a BTC COIN-margined contract is denominated in BTC. 

Please note that unrealized profit and loss are calculated based on the Mark Price, while realized profit and loss are calculated based on the Last Price. 

### Profit and Loss calculations for USDⓈ-M Futures contracts (BTCUSDT)

In USDⓈ-M Futures, stablecoins like USDT are used as margin, and order amounts and position sizes are calculated in coins.

Example 1:

  * You buy a long position of 1 BTC at an opening price of 50,000 USDT.
  * The price rises, and you exit at 55,000 USDT.
  * Profit: (Exit Price - Entry Price) * Contract Size = (55,000 - 50,000) * 1 = 5,000 USDT.

Example 2:

  * You sell (short) 1 BTCUSDT perpetual contract at 50,000 USDT.
  * The price drops, and you exit at 45,000 USDT.
  * Profit: (Exit Price - Entry Price) * Contract Size = (45,000 - 50,000) * -1 = 5,000 USDT.

### Profit and Loss calculations for COIN-M Futures contracts (BTCUSD)

A BTC COIN-M Futures contract is denominated, collateralized, and settled in Bitcoin, which means Bitcoin is used as the base currency. Each BTC COIN-M contract represents 100 USD and as such, USD is the counter currency. Since each contract represents a fixed quantity of USD, this means BTC is used to fund the Initial Margin or calculate profit and loss. 

Suppose you purchased 100 BTC-margined perpetual contracts (100 * $100 = $10,000) at $50,000 each. By doing this, you are essentially selling $10,000 and buying an equivalent value of Bitcoin (10,000 / 50,000 = 0.2 BTC).

Suppose Bitcoin’s price rose to $55,000 and you want to secure profits from the trade. To close the position, you buy back $10,000 worth of contracts and simultaneously sell the equivalent in Bitcoin (10,000 / 55,000 = 0.1818 BTC).

In this trade, your profit will be calculated as: Quantity of Bitcoins at Entry - Quantity of Bitcoins at Exit = 0.2 - 0.1818 = 0.0182 BTC.

In short, the profit and loss formula will be:

((1 / Futures Entry Price) - (1 / Futures Exit Price)) * Contract Size in USD

((1/ 50,000) - (1 / 55,000)) * (100 * 100) = 0.0182 BTC

Example for short position:

Short BTCUSD 0925 Quarterly (Buy USD, Sell BTC): 

((1 / Futures Entry Price) - (1 / Futures Exit Price)) * (Contract Size * -1)

((1/50,000) - (1/45,500)) * (100 contracts * 100 USD * -1) = 0.0198 BTC

### How to calculate Unrealized PNL and ROI percentage?

You can use the Mark Price or the Entry Price to calculate the Return on Investment (ROI). Go to the [Positions] tab on the trading interface, click [PnL(ROI%)] and select the desired price basis.

Image: image

Image: image

#### USDⓈ-M Futures Contracts

  * If you chose the Mark Price as the price basis:

Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Direction of Order * (Mark Price - Entry Price)

ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT / Entry Margin = ( (Mark Price - Entry Price ) * Direction of Order * Contract Size * Absolute Value of the position) / (Contract size * Mark Price * IMR)

*IMR = 1 / Leverage

  * If you chose the Last Price as the price basis:

Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Direction of Order * (Last Price - Entry Price)

ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT / Entry Margin = ( (Last Price - Entry Price) * Direction of Order * Contract Size * Absolute Value of the position) / (Contract size * Mark Price * IMR)

Direction of order: 1 for long orders; -1 for short orders

The ROI% calculation has been updated to provide a more accurate reflection of your trading performance by including all related fees.

ROI = (realizedPNL + commissionFeeTotal + fundingFee + insuranceClearFee) / (entryPrice*openedVolum/leverage)

This means that the ROI now accounts for:

  * Realized Profit and Loss (realizedPNL)
  * Total Commission Fees (commissionFeeTotal)
  * Funding Fees (fundingFee)
  * Insurance Clearing Fees (insuranceClearFee)

By including these fees, the ROI% gives you a clearer picture of your net returns on each position.

#### COIN-M Futures Contracts

Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * Absolute value of Position * Direction of Order * (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Mark Price)

ROI% = Unrealized PNL * price / abs(size) * Contract Multiplier * IMR

Please note that "price" in the above formula could be the Mark Price or the Entry Price (based on the price basis).

### ¿Cómo calcular las PnL no realizadas y el % de ROI?

#### Futuros USDⓈ-M

Precio de marca como referencia de precio:

  * PnL no realizadas = tamaño del contrato × valor absoluto de la posición × dirección de la orden × (precio de marca - precio de entrada)
  * % de ROI = PnL no realizadas en USDT o USDC ÷ margen de entrada = [(precio de marca - precio de entrada) × dirección de la orden × tamaño] ÷ (tamaño del contrato × precio de marca × IMR)
    * IMR = 1 ÷ apalancamiento

Último precio como referencia de precio:

  * PnL no realizadas = tamaño del contrato × valor absoluto de la posición × dirección de la orden × (último precio - precio de entrada)
  * % de ROI = PnL no realizadas en USDT o USDC ÷ margen de entrada = ( (último precio - precio de entrada) × dirección de la orden × tamaño) ÷ (tamaño del contrato × precio de marca × IMR)
    * Dirección de la orden:
      * 1 para órdenes long
      * -1 para órdenes short

El cálculo del % de ROI se actualizó para ofrecer un reflejo más preciso de tu rendimiento de trading al incluir todas las comisiones relacionadas.

ROI = (RealizedPNL + commissionFeeTotal + fundingFee + insuranceClearFee) / (entryPrice*openedVolum/leverage)

Esto significa que el ROI ahora incluye:

  * Ganancias y pérdidas realizadas (realizedPNL)
  * Total de comisiones de trading (commissionFeeTotal)
  * Comisiones de financiación (fundingFee)
  * Comisiones de compensación del seguro (insuranceClearFee)

Al incluir estas comisiones, el % de ROI te da una imagen más clara de tus retornos netos en cada posición.

#### Futuros COIN-M

Precio de marca como referencia de precio:

  * PnL no realizadas = tamaño del contrato × multiplicador del contrato × valor absoluto de la posición × dirección de la orden × (1 ÷ precio de entrada - 1 ÷ precio de marca)
  * % de ROI = PnL no realizadas × precio de marca / abs(tamaño) × multiplicador del contrato × IMR

Último precio como referencia de precio:

  * PnL no realizadas = tamaño del contrato × multiplicador del contrato × valor absoluto de la posición × dirección de la orden × (1 ÷ precio de entrada - 1 ÷ último precio)
  * % de ROI = PnL no realizadas × precio de marca ÷ abs(tamaño) × multiplicador del contrato × IMR

### How to trade on Binance Futures?

1. Log in to your Binance account and go to the USDⓈ-M or COIN-M Futures trading page. If you don’t have a Futures account yet, please refer to "How to Open a Binance Futures Account?".

2. Transfer USDT or USDC to your USDⓈ-M Futures Account, or other coins (e.g., BTC) to your COIN-M Futures Account, as margin.

3. Choose a symbol to trade and select a preferred leverage.

4. Choose an order type and customize the order details. Click [Buy/Long] or [Sell/Short] to place your order.

### How to calculate unrealized PNL and ROI%?

#### USDⓈ-M Futures

Using Mark Price as the price basis:

  * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Order Direction * (Mark Price - Entry Price)
  * ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT or USDC / Entry Margin = ( (Mark Price - Entry Price) * Order Direction * Size) / (Contract Size * Mark Price* IMR)
    * IMR = 1 / Leverage

Using Last Price as the price basis:

  * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Order Direction * (Last Price - Entry Price)
  * ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT or USDC / Entry Margin = ( (Last Price - Entry Price) * Order Direction * Size) / (Contract Size * Mark Price* IMR)
    * Order Direction:
      * 1 for long orders
      * -1 for short orders

The ROI% calculation has been updated to provide a more accurate reflection of your trading performance by including all related fees.

ROI = (RealizedPNL + commissionFeeTotal + fundingFee + insuranceClearFee) / (entryPrice*openedVolum/leverage)

This means that the ROI now accounts for:

  * Realized Profit and Loss (realizedPNL)
  * Total Commission Fees (commissionFeeTotal)
  * Funding Fees (fundingFee)
  * Insurance Clearing Fees (insuranceClearFee)

By including these fees, the ROI% gives you a clearer picture of your net returns on each position.

#### COIN-M Futures

Using Mark Price as the price basis:

  * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * Absolute value of Position * Order Direction * (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Mark Price)
  * ROI% = Unrealized PNL * Mark Price / abs(Size) * Contract Multiplier * IMR

Using Last Price as the price basis:

  * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * Absolute value of Position * Order Direction * (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Last Price)
  * ROI% = Unrealized PNL * Mark Price / abs(Size) * Contract Multiplier* IMR

Meanwhile, for Altcoin contracts, the multiplier is 10 USD.

  * Notional Value

Notional value is the contract value of a Futures contract. For instance, the notional value of BTCUSD Quarterly 0925 is denominated in BTC.

The contract’s notional value is calculated by multiplying the contract unit by the contract multiplier and divided by mark price. Binance Futures uses the notional value to calculate the required margin, trading fee, delivery fee, and PNL.

For example, the notional value of BTCUSD Quarterly 0925 long is

(Contract Size x Contract Multiplier) / Mark Price

= (10 Contracts x 100 USD) / 10,104 USD

= 0.09897 BTC

  * Unrealized and Realized PNL

Realized PNL refers to profits and losses incurred from completed trade transactions. Unrealized PNL refers to profits and losses associated with transactions not yet completed.

For example, when User A opens 10 contracts of BTCUSD Quarterly 0925 long, the unrealized PNL would be 0.0007 BTC. Once User A closed the position, User A is said to have earned 0.0007 BTC of realized PNL.

Unrealized PNL (BTC)

= Contract Size x Contract Multiplier x (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Mark Price)

= 10 Contracts x 100 USD x (1 / 10,104 USD - 1 / 10,175.8 USD)

= 0.0007 BTC

For more contract specifications, please refer to the Contract Specifications of Quarterly Futures Contract.

### How to view my wallet balance on the wallet dashboard?

Hover over the [Wallet] icon and select [USDⓈ-Margined Futures] or [COIN-Margined Futures]. You’ll be redirected to the Futures Wallet dashboard. 

Image: image

Image: image

The COIN-M Wallet displays the total asset balance in BTC, while the USDⓈ-M Wallet displays the total asset balance in USD. 

Please note that the margin balance factors in unrealized PNL. As such, the margin balance will fluctuate in real-time if there are open positions.

You can view the balance of each asset under the [Assets] tab.

Image: image

Notes:

  * Margin Balance = Wallet Balance + Unrealized PNL.
    * Your positions will be liquidated once the Margin Balance ≤ the Maintenance Margin.
  * Wallet Balance = Total Net Transfer + Total Realized Profit + Total Net Funding Fee - Total Commission
  * Unrealized profit and loss on your positions are calculated based on the Mark Price.
  * Available for Order (i.e., Available margin for opening a position):
    * For USDⓈ-M Futures: Available for Order = max(0, crossWalletBalance + ∑cross Unrealized PNL - (∑Cross Initial Margin + ∑Isolated Open Order Initial Margin))
      * Isolated Open Order Initial Margin = abs(Isolated Present Notional) * IMR - abs(Size) * IMR * Mark Price
    * For COIN-M Futures: Available for Order = max(0, CrossWalletBalance + ∑Cross Unrealized PNL - (∑Cross Initial Margin + ∑Isolated Open Order Initial Margin))
      * Isolated Open Order Initial Margin = abs(Isolated Present Notional) * IMR - abs(Size) * Contract Size * IMR / Mark Price
  * Balance (i.e., Wallet Balance) = Total Net Transfer + Total Realized Profit + Total Net Funding Fee - Total Commission

To prevent immediate liquidation, Binance includes open loss as part of the cost required to open a position when the traders place the order. If open loss is not counted, there is a high probability that users’ position will get liquidated immediately once they have placed such orders.

Cost = Initial Margin + Open Loss (if any)

Step 1: Calculate initial margin

Initial Margin

= Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * IMR / Entry Price

= [ (10*100 USD * (1/20)) / 9,800 USD ]

= 0.0051 BTC

Step 2: Calculate open loss

Open Loss = Number of Contract x Contract Multiplier x Absolute Value {min[0, direction of order x (1 / order price - 1 /mark price)]}

*direction of order: 1 for long order；-1 for short order

Open loss of long order

= 10 x 100 USD x Absolute Value {min[0, 1 x (1 / 9,800 USD - 1 / 9,602.6 USD)]}

= 0.002097646 BTC

Open loss of short order

= 10 x 100 USD x Absolute Value {min[0, -1 x (1 / 9,800 USD - 1 / 9,602.6 USD)]}

= 0

Step 3: Calculate the cost required to open a position

Since the long order includes an open loss, the cost required to open a long position is higher, as it accounts for both the initial margin and the open loss.

Cost required to open a long position

= 0.0051 BTC + 0.002096562 BTC

= 0.0072 BTC (difference due to rounding)

The short order has no open loss, so the cost required to open a short position is equivalent to the initial margin.

Cost required to open a short position

= 0.0051 BTC + 0 = 0.0051 BTC
